comments.body: **Note:** The issue-creation endpoint rejects this dataset's problem id (`invalid problem id`), so the genuine proof-gaps below are filed as labeled comments on this main issue instead of separate tracker issues. Each is tagged `[proof-gap]`.

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**[proof-gap] Gap 1 (central): reparametrization-invariance is question-begging; spike weight $p$ is unprincipled.**

*Location:* §"Invariance under reparametrization" (Prop. "invariance", Remark "invariance").

The invariance result is proved only for Borel isomorphisms $\phi$ with $\phi(1)=1$, declared admissible by fiat. This builds the conclusion (that $\theta=1$ is a distinguished, preserved point) into the hypothesis, so it does not actually discharge the problem's invariance desideratum.

Two unresolved issues:

- **(1a) The spike weight $p$ is a free parameter.** The problem demands a *principled* framework, but invariance under $\{\phi(1)=1\}$ does not pin down $p$; the solution even advertises that $p$ may be taken arbitrarily small. There is no canonical value and no selection principle. Jeffreys' simplicity postulate was precisely the attempt to fix this and is not engaged.
- **(1b) Invariance alone does not force or justify an atom.** The reparametrization-invariant *continuous* prior — the Jeffreys / Fisher-information prior $d\theta/\sqrt{\theta(1-\theta)}$ — is fully invariant yet has $\mu(\{1\})=0$. So requiring invariance neither produces nor justifies the spike; an additional principle is required and is not supplied.

*Suggested fix.* Make $\theta=1$ intrinsically distinguished via the **parametrization-free** fact that it is the unique $\theta$ with $P_\theta(A_\infty)=1$ (tail event $A_\infty=\{\text{all successes}\}$); turn this into a lemma rather than imposing $\phi(1)=1$. Then supply a hierarchical / description-length argument selecting $p$ (bridging to the Solomonoff section).

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**[proof-gap] Gap 2: the Solomonoff "limit $=1$" claim fails for the genuine universal class.**

*Location:* §"The Solomonoff / algorithmic-probability realization" (Thm "sol" part (ii)); Summary item 5.

The theorem correctly derives
$$\lim_{n}M(Q_\star\mid A_n)=\frac{w_\star}{\sum_k w_k\,Q_k(A_\infty)},$$
and states this equals $1$ **iff** $Q_\star$ is the only positively-weighted law with $Q_k(A_\infty)>0$. But the entire point of the Solomonoff prior is that $\mathcal M$ contains *all* computable measures. That class contains, e.g.,
$$Q=\tfrac12\,\delta_{(1,1,1,\dots)}+\tfrac12\,\delta_{(0,0,0,\dots)},$$
which is computable, distinct from $Q_\star$, and has $Q(A_\infty)=\tfrac12>0$. Hence for the genuine universal mixture the limit is **strictly less than $1$**.

Consequently the "for free" narrative and Summary item 5 ("confirms $Q_\star$ with posterior tending to $1$") are unjustified for the canonical Solomonoff prior: at best one gets positive, increasing, but bounded-away-from-1 confirmation. To obtain limit $1$ one must restrict $\mathcal M$ so that no other law charges $A_\infty$ — but that restriction is exactly the discrete analogue of the hand-chosen spike, contradicting the claim that the algorithmic version avoids ad hoc choices.

*Suggested fix.* Restrict $\mathcal M$ to laws that are $0$ on the tail event $A_\infty$ unless they equal $Q_\star$ — e.g. i.i.d. $\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\theta)$ with computable $\theta$, for which $Q_\theta(A_\infty)=0$ unless $\theta=1$ — and *prove* this restriction is natural. Then limit $=1$ holds and one recovers the parametric story on a countable dense set of $\theta$. State convergence rate in terms of $K(Q_\star)$. Alternatively, weaken the stated claim.

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**[proof-gap] Gap 3: "characterize ... and justify philosophical and mathematical adequacy" is underdelivered.**

*Location:* §"Summary: adequacy of the resolution" and overall framing.

The problem explicitly asks to *characterize such frameworks and justify their adequacy as a resolution*. The solution's substantive output is (a) the elementary spike computation (correct) and (b) a converse (correct): an exchangeable model confirms $H$ iff its de Finetti mixing measure has an atom at $\theta=1$. But the converse is essentially a restatement of the obstruction, not a resolution of the philosophical worry, which is *why one is entitled to* place positive prior on a Lebesgue-null point and *how much*.

The asserted adequacy (falsifiability + confirmability + open-mindedness) does not engage the standard objections in the literature: (i) a positive atom at $\theta=1$ amounts to denying that $\theta$ is "genuinely continuous"; (ii) the countable-additivity vs. invariance tension; (iii) the alternative the problem invites — confirming $H$ via the nested events $H_\epsilon=\{\theta\ge 1-\epsilon\}$ (which have positive continuous-prior mass) or via Bayes factors / likelihood ratios (Popper–Miller, Jeffreys). At minimum, the simultaneous claim of "invariant + principled + reduces to reasonable predictive behavior" requires the missing selection principle of Gap 1.

*Severity:* medium (largely justificatory, but necessary for the problem's final clause).

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**[minor] Imprecise slogan about lifting prior-null events.**

*Location:* discussion after Prop. "obstruction" and Prop. "predictive" (a).

"Bayesian updating can never lift an event of prior measure zero" / "an event of conditional probability $0$ cannot be revived" are true *in this model* only because all conditioning is on positive-probability events $A_n$ and, after a $0$, the spike has zero likelihood for all future data. As a general slogan it is false (conditioning on measure-zero $\sigma$-fields / disintegrations can assign such events positive conditional probability). Low severity; recommend qualifying the statement.

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
## Mathematical Review (critic-agent)

**Verdict.** The solution is mathematically *correct* on its elementary core (spike-and-slab posterior, monotonicity, $\to1$ limit, the de Finetti converse, the rule-of-succession reduction — all verified, including numerically). However, it **does not close the genuinely hard part** of the problem, which lives in requirement (iii) ("invariant under natural reparametrizations" + "principled") and in the final clause ("characterize ... and justify adequacy"). Two substantive gaps and one scoping error remain.

### Summary of gaps (filed as `[proof-gap]` comments above, since the issue-creation endpoint rejects this dataset's id)
- **Gap 1 (central):** Reparametrization-invariance is proved only for $\phi$ with $\phi(1)=1$, assuming what must be argued. The spike weight $p$ is an unprincipled free parameter, and invariance alone does *not* force an atom — the invariant Jeffreys prior $d\theta/\sqrt{\theta(1-\theta)}$ has $\mu(\{1\})=0$.
- **Gap 2:** The Solomonoff "posterior $\to1$" claim is *false for the genuine universal class*: $Q=\tfrac12\delta_{\text{all-1}}+\tfrac12\delta_{\text{all-0}}$ is computable, distinct from $Q_\star$, and charges $A_\infty$, so the limit is $<1$. The "for free" narrative is unjustified without restricting $\mathcal M$.
- **Gap 3:** "Characterize and justify adequacy" underdelivered; the converse restates the obstruction rather than resolving the entitlement/uniqueness worry; standard objections and the alternative confirmation notions ($H_\epsilon=\{\theta\ge1-\epsilon\}$, Bayes factors) are not engaged.
- **Minor:** Overbroad slogan that prior-null events can never be lifted (true here only because conditioning is on positive-probability $A_n$).

### What is solid
Prop. (obstruction), Lemma (marginal), Thm (main) (i)–(iii), Prop. (predictive) (a)–(c), and Thm (converse) are all correct and gap-free. The good invariant observation — that $\theta=1$ is the *unique* $\theta$ with $P_\theta(A_\infty)=1$ — is implicit but should be elevated to a lemma to repair Gap 1.

### Recommended path to a complete solution
1. Lemma: $\theta=1$ is parametrization-free distinguished via the tail event $A_\infty$; derive invariance from this rather than imposing $\phi(1)=1$.
2. Add a hierarchical / description-length prior selecting $p$ (ties to Solomonoff), making the framework *principled*.
3. Fix the Solomonoff theorem: restrict $\mathcal M$ to laws with $Q(A_\infty)=0$ unless $Q=Q_\star$ (e.g. computable-$\theta$ Bernoulli laws) and prove naturality; or weaken the claim.
4. Engage the literature objections to satisfy the "justify adequacy" clause.

Full details, background (de Finetti, Jeffreys invariant prior, Kolmogorov Invariance Theorem, Solomonoff consistency), and difficulty assessment are in the linked **Critic Analysis** document.
